cards.explanation: The answer is “Send everyone away from me!” Joseph cries that out in Genesis 45:1. He wants the room empty before he makes himself known to his brothers. I've cleared a kitchen for a private moment myself, friends, usually because I dropped a whole tray.

The answer is False. Joseph wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him, and Pharaoh's household soon heard of it (Genesis 45:2). Pharaoh was the king of Egypt, so word went all the way to the top. Clearing the room didn't make it quiet, and I think this man had been holding it in a long time.

The answer is “Is my father still alive?” Joseph says, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?” (Genesis 45:3). After all these years, that's the question he asks first. I think that tells you a lot about this man, friends.

The answer is True. The text says they were unable to answer him, because they were terrified in his presence (Genesis 45:3). Picture it, bakers: the man you wronged turns out to be the ruler in front of you. I think my own mouth would stop working too.

The answer is False. Joseph says, “…do not be distressed or angry with yourselves…” (Genesis 45:5). He's the one who got sold, and he's the one saying it's okay to put the weight down. Nothing in his words shames them.

The answer is to save lives. Joseph says, “…it was to save lives that God sent me before you.” (Genesis 45:5). He doesn't point to a payback or a lesson. The reason he gives is lives being saved, and he says it right to his brothers' faces.

The answer is five. Joseph says five more years are coming, with no plowing and no harvesting (Genesis 45:6). The famine has already covered the land two years, so the hard stretch isn't over yet. Joseph's words come right before he tells his brothers to go and bring their father.

The answer is father. Joseph says God has made him a father to Pharaoh (Genesis 45:8). Pharaoh is the king of Egypt, so that's quite a title to be handed. I don't know how it felt to him, friends, but it's one big seat to sit in.

The answer is that his father should come down to him without delay. Joseph's message says, “Come down to me without delay.” (Genesis 45:9). He wants his father there, and he doesn't want to wait around for it. The man is not interested in a slow RSVP.
The answer is Goshen. Joseph says, “You shall settle in the land of Goshen and be near me…” (Genesis 45:10). He doesn't just want them in Egypt, bakers. He wants them near him.

The answer is True. Joseph says, “…there I will provide for you…” (Genesis 45:11). He gives the reason too: there will be five more years of famine. He isn't only inviting them over, he's promising to feed them.

The answer is all his splendor in Egypt. Joseph says, “Tell my father about all my splendor in Egypt and everything you have seen.” (Genesis 45:13). The brothers are his witnesses, and they've got a lot to report. I'd want my dad to hear every bit of it too.

The answer is Benjamin. The text says Joseph threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and wept (Genesis 45:14). Benjamin was the brother Judah had just begged to protect (Genesis 44:33). It's a tender moment, friends.
The answer is False. The text says Joseph wept, and Benjamin wept as they embraced (Genesis 45:14). Two brothers, two sets of tears. I'd have needed the whole napkin stack.

The answer is that they talk with him. The text says afterward his brothers talked with him (Genesis 45:15). They were unable to answer him earlier, so this is a big change. Silence, then tears, then conversation.

The answer is True. The text says that when the news reached Pharaoh's house that Joseph's brothers had come, Pharaoh and his servants were pleased (Genesis 45:16). Pharaoh was the king of Egypt, and he goes on to tell Joseph what to say to his brothers. That's a warm welcome.

The answer is best. Pharaoh says, “I will give you the best of the land of Egypt…” (Genesis 45:18). Pharaoh is the king of Egypt, so he's offering what he has to give. That is not a leftovers offer, friends.

The answer is wagons. Pharaoh says to “Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your young children and your wives…” (Genesis 45:19). He's thinking about the little ones and the trip home. That's a king who plans ahead.

The answer is False. Pharaoh says, “But pay no regard to your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.” (Genesis 45:20). No need to haul every last thing, because Egypt has it covered. That's a lighter load for the road.

The answer is three hundred shekels and five sets of clothes. Benjamin gets three hundred shekels of silver and five sets of clothes (Genesis 45:22). The other brothers each get new garments, so Benjamin's gift is more. The text doesn't say why, so I'll leave it there.
The answer is quarrel. Joseph says, “Do not quarrel on the way!” (Genesis 45:24). He says it as they leave. Even after all this joy, friends, he gives them a rule for the road.

The answer is False. The brothers tell Jacob, their father, that Joseph is alive and ruling all of Egypt, but Jacob was stunned, for he did not believe them (Genesis 45:26). It's a big claim to hear all at once. The belief comes later.

The answer is that it is revived. The text says the spirit of their father Jacob was revived (Genesis 45:27). It happens when they relay all that Joseph had told them and he sees the wagons Joseph sent. I bet those wagons did a lot of the talking, bakers.

The answer is that he'll go to see Joseph before he dies. Israel says, “I will go to see him before I die.” (Genesis 45:28). Israel is the name God gave Jacob (Genesis 35:10). He's not sending anyone else in his place, he plans to go himself.
